events.body:
## Upgrade vulnerable dependencies

This PR upgrades **1** package in `authkit-node` with known security advisories, each to the release that fixes the most of them while being at least 7 days old (brand-new releases are where supply-chain attacks land).

| Package | From | To | Released | Fixes | Still open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonwebtoken` | 8.5.1 | **9.0.0** | 1403 days ago | [CVE-2022-23539](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-23539), [CVE-2022-23541](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-23541), [CVE-2022-23540](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-23540) | - |

### Dependency files

- `package-lock.json`: rewritten by npm
- `package.json`: the new version ranges, or an override for a package that another one pulls in

Lockfiles were resolved in a throwaway container that held back releases under 7 days old, and every version they add was checked against its registry's release date.

### What changed upstream

Quoted from each package's own changelog (found and read with Tavily), for the releases between the two versions:

- **jsonwebtoken** 8.5.1 → 9.0.0: 1 release, from [jsonwebtoken changelog](https://github.com/auth0/node-jsonwebtoken/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)
  - 9.0.0: “Removed support for Node versions 11 and below.”
  - 9.0.0: “The verify() function no longer accepts unsigned tokens by default.”
  - 9.0.0: “RSA key size must be 2048 bits or greater.”
  - 9.0.0: “Key types must be valid for the signing / verification algorithm”

### Tests

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Before the upgrade | ✅ 5 passed |
| After the version bump | ✅ 5 passed |

---
